Article Title: Rahul Gandhi stands with injured NSUI protesters, says 'nafrat ka jawab pyar se diya jaega'
Article Text:
'Nafrat ka jawab pyar se diya jaega': Rahul Gandhi stands with injured NSUI protesters

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress leader and Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday met NSUI protesters who alleged that they were assaulted by Delhi Police during demonstrations. At a press conference, Rahul introduced a woman protester as “our sherni” and said she had remained unafraid despite being beaten.Another protester played ‘Vaishnava Jana To’ on a flute, saying, “nafrat ka jawab pyar se diya jaega...”“I want to introduce our 'sherni'. She was beaten, but she was not afraid. There was no hatred in her heart,” Rahul said.The woman protester said that a woman police constable, identified as Chanchal Yadav, assaulted her after NSUI workers were detained in buses during a peaceful protest. She said there were around 30-40 protesters in each of the three buses, with two women and 20-30 other NSUI members in her bus.“Yesterday, all NSUI workers were protesting peacefully when we were detained in three buses. There were many of our colleagues, around 30-40 in each bus. In our bus, there were two girls and 20-30 other NSUI colleagues. There was a woman constable in the bus named Chanchal Yadav. After being detained, we tried to get off the bus again through the gate and continue leading the protest.We tried to stop the bus and sat down beneath it so that our protest could somehow continue. But Chanchal Yadav grabbed me tightly by the neck and pushed me, causing me to fall backwards onto the seat. She then scratched my face with her nails, leaving scratches across my face and near my ear. When I resisted her, she slapped me so hard and said, 'Here, take another slap across your face.'”Rahul also spoke about Athira, a student from Kerala studying at Delhi University, who alleged that she sustained injuries to her ear and eye during the police action.“Athira from Kerala has lost her hearing in one ear. She is deaf in one ear because she was struck on that ear. She can no longer hear. Last time I showed you a boy who was blinded. Now, she is deaf in one ear,” Rahul said.Athira alleged that there were no women police personnel on the bus when the protesters were detained. She said she asked for a woman officer to be present during the detention, after which the bus stopped outside the Connaught Place police station.“I am from Kerala, studying at Delhi University. Yesterday, when they detained us, there were no female police officers in the bus. So, I simply asked, 'Where is the lady police officer or lady constable?' If they want to detain us, having at least one female constable present is mandatory. Then, the bus moved and stopped in front of the Connaught Place police station, where they continuously hit my entire cheek. Because of this, I have an injury to my eye and damage to my ear. ”Rahul also condemned the five-day judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, saying that waving the national flag during a peaceful protest was not a crime.Das and Ranka were sent to five-day judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail on Wednesday for allegedly violating their peace bonds and trespassing into Jantar Mantar, which was recently de-notified as a designated protest site, police sources said.Bail bond formalities for their associate Ajinkya Shinde were being finalised, they added.The three CJP leaders were produced before an Executive Magistrate on Wednesday morning. They had been detained on Tuesday after allegedly breaching barricades and entering the protest site without authorisation while raising slogans demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.Police registered a case against the activists on charges including trespassing, violating prohibitory orders, breaching a peace bond and obstructing a public servant from discharging official duties, sources said. Das and Ranka had signed bonds to maintain peace for a year after being detained during a protest on Saturday, they added.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi met NSUI protesters who alleged that they were assaulted by Delhi Police during demonstrations. At a press conference, Rahul introduced a woman protester as “our sherni’ and said she had remained unafraid despite being beaten. He also condemned the five-day judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.

Article Title: 'Don't mess with youth': AAP's Sanjay Singh warns PM Modi after CJP leaders sent to jail
Article Text:
AAP’s Sanjay Singh backs CJP activists after arrest

NEW DELHI: Senior AAP leader and Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Singh on Wednesday warned Prime Minister Narendra Modi against targeting young protesters after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were sent to five days of judicial custody following their detention in an attempt to breach Jantar Mantar.In a post on X, Sanjay accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of opposing the national flag. He questioned the action against the CJP activists for allegedly hoisting the Tricolour and raising slogans at the protest site."Modi-ji, are you British? Is there British rule in India? I know that you people hate the Tricolour; you did not hoist the Tricolour at the RSS headquarters for 52 years. You sent CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to jail for hoisting the Tricolour and chanting "Bharat Mata Ki Jai," he said.Warning the Prime Minister over the activists' judicial custody, Sanjay added, "Do not mess with the youth, Modi-ji; they will soon put an end to your dictatorship."CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke also criticised PM Modi, calling the action against the activists "cowardly tactics".In a post on X, Dipke said, "Ashu and Saurav have been sent to 5 days' judicial custody.Their fault? Unfurling the tricolour at Jantar Mantar. Show some guts, Narendra Modi. If you’re so determined to crush dissent, have the courage to officially declare an Emergency instead of hiding behind these cowardly tactics."CJP activist Ajinkya Shinde, who was also placed under preventive arrest along with Das and Ranka, alleged that the activists were detained for waving the national flag and raising slogans of 'Vande Mataram' and 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai'.Speaking to reporters, Shinde said, "You must know that today Ashutosh, Saurav Das, and I, along with CJP volunteers, went towards Jantar Mantar, and we just waved the Indian flag and shouted Vande Mataram. So for this, this Modi-Shah fascist government has sent Saurav Das and Ashutosh to jail for 5 days," he said.The Delhi Police detained all three CJP activists on Tuesday for allegedly trespassing at Jantar Mantar while attempting to enter the site. The action came a day after authorities de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest location. Police sources said a case had been registered in connection with the incident.Earlier, CJP legal head Ratna Singh alleged that the activists had been denied access to their lawyers for several hours and were not initially informed of the grounds for their detention. She also said the activists were likely to be produced before the relevant magistrate.The developments come amid an ongoing agitation by the CJP and Opposition parties against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.
Article Summary: AAP's Sanjay Singh warns PM Narendra Modi against targeting young protesters. CJP activists Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das sent to five days of judicial custody. Activists detained for allegedly hoisting the Tricolour and raising slogans at protest site.

Article Title: 'Murdering democracy': Opposition slams Centre for the arrest of CJP leaders

NEW DELHI: Opposition leaders on Wednesday slammed the Centre over the arrest of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were sent to five days of judicial custody after protesting at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee called the situation “BJP’s new Pakistanified Bharat”, while leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi said jailing young protesters for waving the Tricolour was “an act of cowardice”.Leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi said waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar during a peaceful protest was not a crime and called jailing the two men “an act of cowardice”.“Students. Youth. Journalists. The INDIA bloc. Different banners, one cause,” he said, adding that the groups were united in demanding their constitutional rights. “Jantar Mantar belongs to the people of India. We will reclaim it.”Former chief minister of Tamil Nadu and DMK president MK Stalin questioned how many protesters the government could detain and how many young voices the BJP could silence. He said jailing more young people would prompt more ordinary citizens, including those without political affiliations, to take to the streets.Stalin expressed solidarity with Das and Ranka and said the DMK was ready to provide them with all necessary legal representation and support.AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal questioned whether waving the national flag in India could be considered a crime.“Is waving our own flag in our own country a crime? This is absolutely ridiculous,” he said.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray said the two CJP leaders had been jailed for holding the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar. Asking when holding the national flag had become a crime for young Indians, he said the fight would continue until democracy was reclaimed.Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee accused the BJP of arresting Indians for unfurling and waving the national flag in their own country. He called the situation “BJP’s new Pakistanified Bharat”.Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee strongly condemned the arrest of CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, calling it an attempt to intimidate and silence an entire generation.“We must never surrender our constitutional rights,” she said, urging people to unite to protect democracy. Banerjee also alleged that 14,000 people in West Bengal were facing police and political atrocities, and said young people could count on her support. “Your Didi is with you — today and forever!” she said.Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra expressed solidarity with the two arrested leaders, writing: “With you boys. We will reclaim this country from these thugs & looteras.”Communist Party of India (CPI) general secretary D Raja called the detention and judicial custody of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka “undemocratic”, alleging that the case over trespassing amounted to harassment.Raja pointed out that Jantar Mantar had been a designated protest site until two days earlier and accused the government of trying to curtail protests and silence dissent out of fear of public anger. He questioned when protesting against an “undemocratic order” had become a crime and demanded the immediate release of the two leaders.Raja said the denotification of Jantar Mantar would be challenged politically and legally. He added that the All India Students’ Federation (AISF) and All India Youth Federation (AIYF) had marched to reclaim the protest site and would intensify their struggle to restore the right to protest.Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained early Tuesday after allegedly breaching barricades and entering Jantar Mantar, recently denotified as a designated protest site, while raising slogans demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.They were sent to five days of judicial custody on Wednesday.Police have booked them on charges including trespassing, violating prohibitory orders, breaching a peace bond and obstructing a public servant. The arrests came amid protests by CJP and other organisations over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Opposition leaders slam the Centre over the arrest of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. The two men were sent to five days of judicial custody after protesting at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

NEW DELHI: NCP(SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande sharply criticised the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, calling the preventive arrest 'bizarre'. Gawande also said Rahul Gandhi had asked the INDIA bloc to be ready at 24 hours’ notice for further protests, as the bloc seeks Supreme Court intervention over the arrests and other concerns related to the Election Commission.He questioned the trespassing FIR against them and asked Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar whether he supported the action against young protesters at Jantar Mantar.“This preventive arrest is bizarre. What is the actual complaint? Trespassing, filed by the JD(U)?” Gawande said, calling it a “sad day for the JD(U) and an even sadder day for Indian democracy”.Das and Ranka were detained early Tuesday after allegedly breaching barricades and entering Jantar Mantar, recently denotified as a designated protest site, while raising slogans demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The police case includes charges of trespassing, violating prohibitory orders, breaching a peace bond and obstructing a public servant.Gawande invoked Nitish Kumar’s background in student politics and the JP movement, asking whether the Bihar chief minister supported the FIR against young people who, he said, were trying to wave the national flag at Jantar Mantar.He also said the INDIA bloc had been asked by leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi to remain ready at 24 hours’ notice for further protests.The bloc expects the Supreme Court to address what Gawande described as an illegal FIR, alleged police brutality and concerns over the functioning of the Election Commission, including Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The arrest follows protests by CJP and other organisations over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. On October 11, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar designated Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as venues for demonstrations, removing Jantar Mantar from the list of approved protest sites. CJP has argued that shifting protests away from the capital’s political centre reduces the visibility of dissent.
Article Summary: CP(SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande sharply criticised the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. He questioned the trespassing FIR against them and asked Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar whether he supported the action against young protesters. Gawande also said Rahul Gandhi had asked the INDIA bloc to be ready at 24 hours’ notice for further protests.

NEW DELHI: BJP has dismissed allegations made by the Trinamool Congress ( TMC ) that a woman attempted to attack former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee with a knife outside her residence in Kolkata.The BJP dismissed the allegations, with West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh taking a swipe at Banerjee and questioning her claims of being attacked.“She herself makes such claims all the time. Article Title: 'Heights of irony': Congress hits back at Amit Shah over 2029 poll claim with '3 Bs'

NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday hit back at Union home minister Amit Shah over his prediction of a resounding victory for the BJP-led NDA in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Taking a dig at Shah, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal described his remarks as the “heights of irony”, questioning why the home minister was celebrating electoral victories while the opposition was protesting against alleged irregularities in the electoral system.“Heights of irony that Vote Chor Amit Shah is celebrating an election victory - when the whole problem is how they are destroying our electoral system,” Venugopal wrote on X.He also questioned Shah's focus on the 2029 elections, claiming that the home minister's remarks reflected concerns about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's political position. Venugopal further alleged that Shah appeared nervous during his interaction with the media, claiming that he spoke only to what he called “Godi media” and did not take questions.“Mr. Shah, you should certainly be worried about surviving in office till 2029,” Venugopal added.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh also targeted Shah, reviving the opposition's allegations of vote theft and accusing the home minister of relying on rhetoric rather than addressing concerns over the electoral process.“The Union home minister is back with his 3 Bs—Bombast, Bluff and Bluster,” Ramesh wrote on X.Calling Shah the “co-architect of Vote Chori”, Ramesh alleged that the BJP had already begun preparing to manipulate the 2029 elections.“The people know that the Constitutional right vote is their biggest power to hold authoritarian governments built on lies - like this one - accountable and send them packing,” he wrote, adding that the youth were among those taking to the streets.The Congress leaders' remarks came after Shah, in his first comments on the ongoing protests demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation and the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, predicted another crushing defeat for the Congress in 2029.Shah accused Rahul Gandhi and the opposition of pursuing negative politics, arguing that the Congress needed to introspect over its repeated electoral defeats. He maintained that voters continued to support PM Modi, the BJP and the NDA, citing recent bypolls and local body election results as evidence.Opposition leaders, including Rahul and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, joined INDIA bloc allies in a march for democracy in Delhi on Monday and vowed to continue their resistance against alleged electoral irregularities.
Article Summary: Congress general secretary KC Venugopal described his remarks as the “heights of irony” He also questioned Shah's focus on the 2029 elections, claiming that the home minister's remarks reflected concerns about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's political position. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh also targeted Shah, reviving the opposition's allegations of vote theft.

Article Title: L Murugan writes to PM Modi seeking exit from Union Cabinet, says wants to return to grassroots
Article Text:
L Murugan

NEW DELHI: Union minister of state for Information and Broadcasting L Murugan has sought to step down from the Union Council of Ministers and relinquish his Rajya Sabha membership, saying he wants to return to grassroots politics.Murugan said he intends to devote himself full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu and preparing the party for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.In a letter addressed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Murugan said he wished to focus on expanding the party’s presence across the state. He also shared the letter on X, reiterating his commitment to working with party workers.“With humility and a grateful heart, I therefore request you to relieve me of my responsibilities as Minister of State and permit me to relinquish my membership of the Rajya Sabha, so that I may dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the party in Tamil Nadu,” Murugan wrote in the letter.He added, “I want to go to every village and every street, meet our people, stand beside our karyakartas and help expand the party's presence in every part of the State.”In his post on X, Murugan said, “It has been the greatest honour of my life to serve Bharat Mata and Tamil Nadu under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi.”“Now, I wish to return to the grassroots, stand with our karyakartas and dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections,” he added.Murugan also expressed gratitude to Modi for giving him the opportunity to serve in the Union government, highlighting his background as the son of daily wage labourers.“I do not come from a political family. I come from a very poor family. My parents, who worked as daily wage labourers and cattle grazers, continue to lead a simple life in Konur village,” he wrote.Reflecting on his political journey, Murugan said his guiding principle over nearly three decades in the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the BJP had remained: “Nation First, Party Next, Self Last.”Murugan has served as minister of state for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs. From July 2021 to June 2024, he also held the portfolios of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying alongside Information and Broadcasting. He previously served as vice-chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes from 2017 to 2020 and as BJP Tamil Nadu president.
Article Summary: L Murugan has sought to step down from the Union Council of Ministers and relinquish his Rajya Sabha membership. He said he intends to devote himself full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu and preparing the party for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. He also shared the letter on X, reiterating his commitment to working with party workers.

Article Title: ‘Get ready to lose 2029 polls’: Amit Shah warns Rahul Gandhi with Congress poll history

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday said Congress leader Rahul Gandhi should “introspect” rather than blame the Election Commission (EC) or the SIR exercise for the opposition party’s electoral setbacks, citing its defeats in the recent byelections and the Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation polls."I also wish to ask Rahul ji: is this the result of an 'SIR'? You dismiss the popularity of the BJP and Modi ji by attributing it to an 'SIR'. You need to introspect," Shah said.Shah also highlighted the Congress's continued poll losses in Gujarat, pointing to its defeat in the Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation polls, held in the state capital.“In a major state (Gujarat) where you (Rahul Gandhi) once held power, you have failed to win a single election in 41 years. This is a matter that demands serious introspection on their (Congress') part,” the senior BJP leader added.The home minister then listed the BJP's victories in the byelections to the Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats in West Bengal and the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency in Assam, where the party's candidates won by large margins in last week's bypolls.He also mentioned the Thattanchavady assembly seat in Puducherry, the byelection for which was won by the BJP's ally, the All India NR Congress."Recently, byelections were held in Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. I want to inform the people of the country today that the Congress party did not win a single seat. In Nagaon, the BJP candidate won by a margin of 1,42,000 votes, wresting the seat from the Congress. In Nandigram, the BJP candidate won with 76% of the vote, securing a massive lead of 1,22,000 votes. In Rejinagar, the BJP won by over 75,000 votes, snatching the seat from the Trinamool, while in Puducherry, the NDA candidate from ally AINRC won by 8,482 votes. The Congress secured only 22% of the votes," Shah said.He also predicted that the BJP-led NDA would secure a massive majority in the 2029 Lok Sabha polls and the Congress would suffer another "crushing defeat.""I want to tell Rahul Gandhi that the people of this country have fully understood your strategy of shielding infiltrators under the guise of the SIR, and they will no longer fall for your ruses. I also wish to tell Shri Rahul and his associates to brace themselves for a crushing defeat in 2029. The NDA is set to secure a massive majority in the 2029 general elections, and the Congress is headed for yet another defeat, its fourth consecutive loss," he remarked.Shah's remarks came shortly after leaders of the Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc held a joint press conference at Rahul Gandhi's residence in New Delhi, where they vowed to continue their campaign for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the invalidation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls over alleged irregularities in the exercise.The Indian Express reported last month that the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had raised objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those related to the SIR.The report brought further scrutiny on Kumar, who has repeatedly been accused by the opposition of facilitating “vote chori” (vote theft) in favour of the BJP since becoming CEC in 2025.Responding to Amit Shah, Congress MP Jairam Ramesh called him a "co-architect of vote-chorti" and claimed that both the home minister and Prime Minister Narendra Modi were "rattled seeing the surge of sentiment against them.""The Union Home Minister is back with his 3 Bs—Bombast, Bluff and Bluster. The co-architect of Vote Chori has, not surprisingly, ‘predicted’ the 2029 Lok Sabha election for which undoubtedly he has already begun the rigging process. But it is not going to happen. The people know that the Constitutional right vote is their biggest power to hold authoritarian governments built on lies - like this one - accountable and send them packing. This is why India, especially the youth, is now out on the streets," Ramesh wrote on X."The diabolical duo is clearly rattled seeing the surge of sentiment against them both across all sections of society in the nation. The HM should start preparing to defend himself from the investigations that will start into his many nefarious deeds when the regime presided over by his Sahib fall," he added.
Article Summary: Congress MP Jairam Ramesh called Amit Shah a "co-architect of vote-chorti" and claimed that the home minister and Prime Minister were "rattled seeing the surge of sentiment against them" The home minister also predicted that the BJP-led NDA would secure a massive majority in the 2029 Lok Sabha polls and the Congress would suffer another "crushing defeat"

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) members, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, have been sent to five days of judicial custody, while party representative Ajinkya Shinde has been was bound down, after 14 party members allegedly trespassed into Jantar Mantar and obstructed police personnel on duty. Delhi Police said the action was prompted by repeated alleged violations of law and concerns that the accused could again disturb public peace and instigate others through social media.Two FIRs have been registered, including one under the section relating to criminal conspiracy.DCP (New Delhi) Sachin Sharma said on Oct 13 , during the morning hours, Das, Ranka, Shinde and 11 other members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) reached Jantar Mantar, which has been denotified as designated protest site, by trespassing through a private premise."Police personnel deployed at the spot intervened and attempted to stop them. After considering the matter, the SEM court, considering the kalandra (preventive legal measure) details and in view of their repeated violations of law, and serious apprehension that if released on bail they will again violate law and instigate others to violate law remanded Das and Ranka to five days of judicial custody.Shinde was bound down to maintain peace and good behaviour for six months on personal bond and surety of Rs 5000.Being bound down means the individuals are required to appear before the investigating officer whenever called and must inform the police before leaving the city.The FIR invoke sections 223, which deals with disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant, 332 (house-trespass in order to commit an offence) and 61 (2) (criminal conspiracy) of BNS at Connaught Place police station.The second FIR was registered under sections 221 (obstructing public servant in discharge of his public functions), 115 (voluntarily causing hurt), 132 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty), 121 (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty) and 3 (5) (common intention) of BNS at Parliament Street police station.

NEW DELHI: Union minister L Murugan on Tuesday offered to resign from the Cabinet and Rajya Sabha, saying he wanted to return to politics in his home state, Tamil Nadu, after being part of govt for over five years. This rekindled the buzz that PM Modi could be preparing to reshuffle his council of ministers amid a steady exit of its members and some being in the queue.Murugan has three and a half years left of his RS term, and his exit will allow BJP to pick a new face from Madhya Pradesh, where he was elected from in 2024.In his five-page letter, Murugan expressed gratitude to the PM for all the opportunities he got and his govt's work for Tamil Nadu. He said, "I therefore request you to relieve me of my responsibilities as Minister of State and permit me to relinquish my membership of the Rajya Sabha so that I may dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the party in Tamil Nadu."What stoked curiosity in political circles is that he chose to post the letter offering his resignation on social media, apparently with the consent of the BJP leadership. This suggested a clear signal from the party brass, leaving many within the governing alliance wondering if it was a prelude to more resignations.L Murugan's exit comes on heels of BJP not renominating ministers Hardeep Puri and B L Verma for another term in RS. Ravneet Bittu and George Kurian have already resigned earlier under similar circumstances.Two other ministers, Pankaj Chaudhary and Harsh Malhotra, have been made chiefs of BJP units in UP and Delhi, making their departure only a matter of time.Interestingly, an imminent RS vacancy from MP opens up the possibility for Puri, the lone Sikh face in the govt, to return to Rajya Sabha.Murugan has been BJP chief in Tamil Nadu, the last one among big states where BJP remains on the margins of electoral politics, and it was given a jolt when K Annamalai, who enjoyed a decent following, quit in June 2026.

NEW DELHI: Taking cognisance of allegations that women journalists were sexually harassed by police personnel while covering the Oct 10 protest for resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Supreme Court Tuesday asked Delhi Police to depute a senior officer to the court on Thursday to respond to the charges.Senior advocate Indira Jaising said that 'Network of Women in Media' has filed a petition narrating the incidents of sexual harassment of women reporters during the anti-SIR protest on Saturday.When Jaising said she has already served an advance copy of the petition to solicitor general Tushar Mehta, who is representing Delhi Police, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "We would like some senior police officer to remain present in the court to explain and assist the court."The day also saw senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia and Mahesh Jethmalani mentioning a petition seeking initiation of criminal contempt action against political leaders for storming SC on Monday evening and obstructing access to SC's petition filing counter, thus blocking the access to justice. The reference was clearly to leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc members who were part of a procession to SC on Monday.Bhatia and Jethmalani sought a ban on political activity inside the court's premises and preservation of CCTV footage of Monday evening.During an extraordinary hearing on Sunday - on the Oct 10 protest - SC had found authorities to have prima facie breached its Oct 9 order restraining complete closure of metro stations and train services in the capital on the day of protest.It had sought responses from Union home secretary, Delhi Police commissioner and Delhi Metro chief on contempt petitions filed against them. It had also sought a status report from police on petitions accusing use of excessive force on protesters, who were not allowed to assemble at Jantar Mantar.More journalists, senior advocate G Sankaranarayanan said, have filed contempt petitions, two of them, as well as a writ petition related to the protest. SC had directed that professional activities of lawyers, journalists and other professionals would not be hindered. He said the issues are serious.The CJI Kant-led bench said, "Of course all the issues raised in all the petitions are serious and we would like to examine them." On the alleged manhandling of advocates Shadan Farasat, Dinesh Dwivedi and Uttara Babar, a separate petition by lawyers was mentioned by senior advocate C U Singh.While a clutch of petitions were in favour of the street protest and castigating police action in not permitting protest at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10, there were a few stood out as they questioned the protest, its modus operandi and serious disruptions it caused in the city, hindering free movement of the silent majority and impeding their daily work.Given the rush of petitions to SC and the fact that Justice Mohana was attending court despite having fever, CJI Kant said all petitions would be taken for hearing Thursday. The bench also accepted the solicitor general's request for extension of time till Thursday for home secretary, Delhi Police commissioner and Delhi Metro chief to file their responses.Senior advocate Nithya Ramakrishnan, appearing for Apoorvanand Jha, alleged that students who were detained by police on Oct 10 were tortured in police custody.
Article Summary: Senior advocate Indira Jaising said that 'Network of Women in Media' has filed a petition narrating the incidents of sexual harassment of women reporters during the anti-SIR protest on Saturday. Article Title: 'Whistle-blower' CRPF officer seeks probe into 'mistreatment' of protesters

NEW DELHI: A serving CRPF officer posted in Manipur has approached National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), National Commission for Women (NCW) and Delhi Police commissioner, seeking an impartial enquiry into three videos circulated on social media, where certain CAPF and police personnel appear to be "physically mistreating" women protesting against SIR and CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi.CRPF assistant commandant Rahul Solanki, who has a history of playing vigilante and whistle-blower, having alleged poor living conditions of CRPF personnel deployed in Jharkhand for 2019 assembly poll and more recently claiming "unauthorised sale" of track suits at CRPF group centre in Greater Noida, clarified in his letter that he was submitting the complaint "in my individual capacity as a concerned citizen of India, committed to the rule of law, and the dignity and safety of women".Sharing three video links that form the basis of his complaint dated Oct 11, he requested an impartial probe and forensic verification of the incident and the circumstances. He added a disclaimer, saying the videos were obtained by him strictly for verification purposes and had not been authenticated. Solanki insisted that he was not endorsing the views and statements of any individuals or organisations behind the videos.Seeking any genuine misconduct on part of the police/CAPF personnel to be addressed fairly, he said in case the allegations of inappropriate behaviour towards women protesters are substantiated, appropriate legal and departmental action may follow against the personnel and their supervisors. Alternatively, if the footage is found to be fabricated or manipulated, legal action and removal of the misleading content, should be pursued as per law.He also requested gender sensitivity training for police personnel on the ground.A CRPF official told TOI that Solanki's act of directly approaching the rights watchdogs and Delhi Police against the conduct of CAPF/police officers, rather than raise the matter with his superiors, may be viewed as indiscipline as service conduct rules bar officers from filing public complaints against govt officers/depts. "The officer concerned was not even on the ground (where protests were held). If he was concerned, he would have raised the matter internally with his superiors," said an officer. The officer hinted that Solanki could face departmental proceedings over violation of conduct rules.
Article Summary: CRPF assistant commandant Rahul Solanki has a history of playing vigilante and whistle-blower. He has alleged poor living conditions of CRPF personnel deployed in Jharkhand for 2019 assembly poll and more recently claimed "unauthorised sale" of track suits at CRPF group centre in Greater Noida.

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal, who heads the joint parliamentary committee examining Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, Tuesday said major provisions of the proposed legislation had the same clauses that were incorporated in the law enacted by UPA govt in 2010.He said this after a meeting of the committee, which interacted with Hindu, Christian and other groups and listened to their views on the proposed legislation facing stiff opposition from certain sections and opposition parties.Jaiswal said the 2010 Act had given power to the home secretary and the principal secretary of the state to confiscate properties of an NGO receiving foreign funding under FCRA if there were irregularities while the new bill proposed to give the same power to a designated authority."The law brought by the UPA govt had decided that if irregularities were found under FCRA, all the assets would be handed over to the home secretary or principal secretary concerned of the state. However, today, there is a designated authority in place of that arrangement," he added.He said those who gave their views to the committee Tuesday included representatives of Syro Malabar Church, Ramakrishna Math and ISKCON among others."Everyone presented their views. We listened carefully to what everyone had to say. When we sit in our committee meeting, we will discuss these matters. We have heard everyone out, and subsequently, we will deliberate on all these points during the committee meeting. We will take the decisions together," Jaiswal said.The bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 and referred to the JPC on Aug 12 following consistent demands of the opposition parties, which alleged that certain provisions of the legislation were highly objectionable.Opposition parties allege that the FCRA Bill targets minorities as certain provisions will choke legitimate funding for Christian NGOs and minority-run social welfare and educational institutions.Govt has rejected the charges and challenged the opposition to identify even one provision that discriminates against minorities. It has also maintained that the proposed legislation is not religion-specific and is aimed at regulating foreign contributions.While introducing the bill in Lok Sabha, Union minister of state for home Nityanand Rai had said the legislation aimed at ensuring proper utilisation of funds received from abroad. Article Summary: BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal said major provisions of the proposed legislation had the same clauses that were incorporated in the law enacted by UPA govt in 2010. Article Title: 'Drunk, armed with knife, hurled abuses': How woman allegedly tried to attack Mamata Banerjee
Article Text:
Anusua Saha, who attacked former CM Mamata Banerjee





KOLKATA: A drunk civic volunteer, armed with a knife, came within a few metres of former chief minister Mamata Banerjee as she stepped out of her Kalighat home on Tuesday to inaugurate a Durga Puja , the first by her this season. After an FIR was lodged, Kalighat police detained Tannishtha Saha for questioning. Banerjee is a Z-plus protectee.In her police complaint, Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen said that around 6 pm, Saha “reportedly known as civic volunteer and a drug addict” approached Banerjee violently and tried to attack her with a knife and claimed to be her niece. She hurled abuses at Banerjee and even lay down on the road, the complaint said.Kolkata Police did not issue a formal statement but a senior officer at Lalbazar said they are in the process of launching an investigation. “We are trying to fix the sequence of events. The accused has been detained and an FIR is being drawn up. We are speaking to eyewitnesses, including those in her security. We have also collected CCTV footage from the area,” he said.Banerjee was heading to the Kalighat Milan Sangha pandal near her residence to inaugurate the puja. Several others were walking along with her when the alleged attempted attack took place.The former CM remained unfazed after the incident and walked down to the pandal, where she summoned a child to cut the ribbon. She offered prayers and was seen chatting with the locals.“Such an attack on a former CM who enjoys Z+ security right outside her residence is unprecedented. An independent probe must be carried out to ascertain if this was pre-planned,” said former KMC MMiC Baiswanor Chattopadhyay, adding that this was the second attack on Banerjee after the one in Halisahar, where her vehicle was vandalised on Aug 9.Trinamool national spokesperson Saket Gokhale said, “A drug addict reached Mamata Banerjee’s residence today and tried to attack her with a knife. This is the condition in Bengal where even a Z+ protectee and 3-time CM is not safe. Was this a planned conspiracy by BJP because Didi is determined to finish them off in Delhi?”
Article Summary: A drunk civic volunteer, armed with a knife, came within a few metres of former chief minister Mamata Banerjee as she stepped out of her Kalighat home. Tannishtha Saha was detained for questioning. Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen said that around 6 pm, Saha “reportedly known as civic volunteer and a drug addict’ approached Banerzee violently and tried to attack her.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi after party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody, alleging that the action was aimed at suppressing dissent.Dipke claimed that the two leaders’ only fault was unfurling the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar and challenged Modi to formally declare an Emergency if the government intended to curb protests.In a post on X, Dipke accused the government of using coercive measures against those demonstrating against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Ashu and Saurav have been sent to 5 days judicial custody. Their fault? Unfurling tricolour at Jantar Mantar. Show some guts, @narendramodi. If you’re so determined to crush dissent, have the courage to officially declare an Emergency instead of hiding behind these cowardly tactics,” he posted.Das and Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody after being detained early Tuesday for allegedly breaching barricades and entering Jantar Mantar, which was recently denotified as a designated protest site.The two allegedly raised slogans demanding Kumar’s resignation.Police registered a case against them on charges including trespassing, violating prohibitory orders, breaching a peace bond and obstructing a public servant from discharging official duties.Das and Ranka had signed bonds undertaking to maintain peace for a year after being detained during an earlier protest in the capital on Saturday, officials said.The latest action comes amid a continuing standoff between the CJP and Delhi Police over the venue for demonstrations against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On October 11, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar issued an order designating Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as venues for protests and demonstrations, following which Jantar Mantar was removed from the list of designated protest sites.The CJP has criticised the decision, arguing that shifting demonstrations away from the political centre of the national capital would diminish the visibility of public dissent.The party has continued to demand Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke criticises Prime Minister Narendra Modi. CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody. Dipke claimed that the two leaders’ only fault was unfurling Tricolour at Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: Accused in Punjab anti-drug activist's murder arrested in Rajasthan
Article Text:
Parvinder Singh Jhota was shot dead in Mansa district after confronting Ashwani Kumar over drug sales.





MANSA: Ashwani Kumar, medical store owner at Mansa, has been arrested from Salasar in Rajasthan. Kumar is main accused in the killing of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh Jhota, who was shot dead on Tuesday morning after he had an altercation with the chemist over sale of banned medicines. Kumar had fled after the incident on Tuesday morning.While the police had arrested Kumar’ cousin Vipin but Ashwani remained at large. The various police teams had been dispatched to arrest him. A police party succeeded in arresting him from Rajasthan.The protesters at Mansa had announced not to perform last rites till justice is delivered and the main accused are arrested. The protesters had given a call for Punjab bandh against the killing of anti-drug activist, for October 15.The police said the main accused has been arrested.
Article Summary: Ashwani Kumar, medical store owner at Mansa, has been arrested from Salasar in Rajasthan. Kumar is main accused in the killing of anti-drug activist Parwinder Singh Jhota. Kumar had fled after the incident on Tuesday morning.

Article Title: Delhi Police register 4 FIRs over INDIA bloc march; seek takedown of 500 pieces of content
Article Text:
Led by leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, top functionaries of the INDIA bloc and supporters had gathered at Barakhamba Road and marched to Supreme Court

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your view on the use of prohibitory orders during public gatherings? They are necessary for public safety They may restrict freedom of expression They should be evaluated case by case 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have registered four FIRs in connection with INDIA bloc's protest on Monday, allegedly over violation of prohibitory orders clamped in the area. Police sources said the cases pertained to alleged breaking of barricades and defacement of roads. Two of the FIRs were registered at Tilak Marg police station, while Mandir Marg and Barakhamba Road stations registered one FIR each.Separately, four FIRs have been registered by Delhi Police over an alleged disinformation campaign, with investigators suspecting Pakistan-based social media handles of attempting to exploit the ongoing protests to spread anti-India narratives and to disturb communal harmony. They have also written to social media platforms seeking the removal of 500-odd pieces of objectionable and misleading content.More than 100 suspicious social media handles, several of which are believed to be operating from Pakistan, are on the police radar.Sources said intelligence agencies and police have found that several social media accounts allegedly operated from across the border have been circulating old and edited videos of riots and violent incidents, falsely portraying them as footage of recent protests in Delhi.Fake social media accounts were created in the name of Indian youths to lend credibility, and to make it seem that the content had originated from within the country, one of the officers said.On Oct 10, several social media handles circulated claims that widespread violence had erupted during the demonstrations in Delhi. An X handle claimed Tuesday that the Army had been deployed in Delhi and markets shut down. Delhi Police responded, saying the video “is out of context and has nothing to do with current events”.On the INDIA bloc protest Monday, police said prohibitory orders under Section 163 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force at the time, making the gathering unauthorised. Police said the restrictions were imposed to prevent unauthorised assemblies and maintain law and order in the area. “As the section was already in force, the gathering was illegal,” a source said.Led by leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, top functionaries of the INDIA bloc and supporters had gathered at Barakhamba Road and marched to Supreme Court where a petition was filed. Thousands of people turned out on the roads between Connaught Place and Supreme Court, waving flags and shouting slogans demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and a halt to the SIR process.On Bhagwan Das Road, many climbed onto a line of parked police vehicles and buses, shouting and cheering as the INDIA bloc politicians waved back at them. Flags of NSUI, Youth Congress, AISA, AISF and SP fluttered above the crowd. Police then began directing the supporters to one side. People started pushing and pulling as security personnel — officers said more than 10,000 personnel had been deployed in and around New Delhi — moved into the crowd.
Article Summary: Delhi Police have registered four FIRs in connection with INDIA bloc's protest on Monday, allegedly over violation of prohibitory orders clamped in the area. Four FIRs have also been registered by Delhi Police over an alleged disinformation campaign. Investigators suspect Pakistan-based social media handles of attempting to exploit the ongoing protests.

Article Title: Man with 14 cases to his name shot dead by assailants
Article Text: New Delhi: A man with 14 criminal cases to his name was found dead in outer Delhi’s Ranhola Sunday. The deceased, Mosin Khan, was a resident of Vikas Nagar in Delhi and had been classified as a bad character at Ranhola police station.Police received information at around 5.30 pm on Oct 11 regarding a man with gunshot injuries. He was taken to a hospital where doctors declared him dead.A purported video of the incident circulating online shows a man entering a narrow street on a bike before stopping at a T-point. Four bike-borne assailants then enter the street and drive up to the victim, with one of them shooting at Mosin from behind. Following this, another man fires multiple shots from the side, after which the two attackers run away from the spot. A bystander tries to grab one of the attackers in vain. After the attack, Mohsin can be seen lying on the ground, asking for help from locals.Analysing CCTV footage in the area, police have identified the suspects, and efforts are being made to apprehend the accused at the earliest. A case has been filed. Further investigation is in progress.
Article Summary: Mosin Khan was a resident of Vikas Nagar in Delhi and had been classified as a bad character at Ranhola police station. A purported video of the incident circulating online shows a man entering a narrow street on a bike before stopping at a T-point. After the attack, Mohsin can be seen lying on the ground, asking for help from locals.

Article Title: Now Mumbai crime branch to probe fake caste certificate case
Article Text:
The court directed the Mumbai Police Commissioner to transfer the case for further examination (Representative image)





MUMBAI: The city crime branch has taken over the investigation into a two decade old case involving former BMC corporator Ramesh Kamble who is accused of contesting the 2002 civic election using forged caste certificate, following directions from the Bombay High Court.The case pertains to a complaint lodged by advocate Chitra Salunkhe who had initially lodged an FIR of cheating, forgery, breach of trust and criminal breach of trust.The Chembur police had initially registered the case early this year. The Chembur police completed their investigation and submitted the closure report with the original investigation papers before the 11th Metropolitan Magistrate court, Kurla classifying it as a 'C' summary closure report stating that the complaint is neither true nor false or complaint filed due to mistake or misunderstanding.Dissatisfied over the probe Chitra had filed writ petition following which the HC directed the police to hand over the probe to some other agency.The complainant Chitra subsequently approached the Bombay High Court through Criminal Writ Petition, seeking re-investigation by another agency. The High Court last month directed the Mumbai Police Commissioner to transfer the investigation to another department.Police commissioner then transferred the case to the Joint commissioner of police (Crime) to conduct the further investigation and filed a report.The complaint alleges that Kamble, who contested the 2002 BMC election from a seat reserved for Scheduled Castes, allegedly submitted a caste certificate claiming to be a Hindu Mahar despite allegedly being a Christian by birth. He subsequently won the election and served as a corporator.According to the complaint, the Divisional Caste Verification Committee, Konkan Bhavan, had declared his caste certificate invalid in 2005. The Bombay High Court and subsequently the Supreme Court also upheld the findings of the caste verification committee. "The case has just been referred to us. We will now examine the allegations, documents and circumstances surrounding the alleged use of the caste certificate and the earlier investigation conducted by Chembur police. '' said an official.
Article Summary: Ramesh Kamble is accused of contesting the 2002 civic election using forged caste certificate. The case pertains to a complaint lodged by advocate Chitra Salunkhe. The Chembur police had initially registered the case early this year.
