Article Title: Minor’s newborn sold for Rs 40,000; Mumbai hospital sealed, FIR against mother, doctor, 4 others
Article Text:
17-year-old girl reportedly sold her newborn for Rs 40,000 after an illegal delivery at a private hospital (Representative image)





NALASOPARA: A newborn was allegedly sold for Rs 40,000 a day after a 17-year-old girl gave birth at a private hospital in Nalasopara, exposing a suspected case of illegal premature delivery and child trafficking . Tulinj police have registered a case against the 22-year-old man accused of raping the minor, her mother, a woman neighbour, the doctor who allegedly conducted the delivery and the couple who allegedly bought the baby.The minor, a resident of Nalasopara East, was in a relationship with the 22-year-old man who lives in the same locality. She became pregnant, and after her mother learnt about it, she was admitted to Surya Hospital in Santosh Bhuvan, Nalasopara East, on Sunday.Police said Dr Shaheen Shaikh allegedly conducted an illegal premature delivery. The newborn was allegedly sold to a couple from Nalasopara for Rs 40,000 the following day. The girl was discharged from the hospital and returned home.On Monday, she complained of abdominal pain and was taken to Tulinj Hospital, run by the Vasai-Virar Municipal Corporation, for treatment. The doctors’ examination revealed she had recently delivered a baby. The hospital authorities informed Tulinj police on Monday night, following which an investigation was launched.Police inspector Marathe of Tulinj police station said a case had been registered against the man accused of raping the minor, her mother, their woman neighbour and the couple who allegedly purchased the newborn.The accused man has been arrested under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act and remanded in police custody till Saturday.Senior Inspector Vijay Jadhav of Tulinj police station said the couple who allegedly bought the baby had been childless for 14 years.Following the incident, the Vasai-Virar Municipal Corporation sealed Surya Hospital. Nilesh Deshmukh, chairman of the civic body’s health department, said strict action would be taken against those involved in conducting illegal deliveries.
Article Summary: 17-year-old girl allegedly sold her newborn for Rs 40,000 after an illegal delivery at a private hospital in Nalasopara. Tulinj police have registered a case against the man accused of raping the minor, her mother, a woman neighbour, the doctor who allegedly conducted the delivery and the couple who allegedly bought the baby.

Article Title: 'PM Modi's problem is not with Jantar Mantar as a location, but with protests': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke
Article Text:
“You cannot denotify the resistance, Narendra Modi,” Dipke said in the post.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday said protests would continue across the country until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigned, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was afraid of public protests.Reacting to the de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, Dipke said the move would not stop demonstrations, but lead to similar protest sites emerging across the country."Narendra Modi's fear is evident from the fact that he has removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. He thinks protests will stop if Jantar Mantar is no longer a designated protest site, but that is not going to happen. Jantar Mantars will now emerge across the country," Dipke said."Narendra Modi's problem is not with Jantar Mantar as a location, but with protests. We must understand this," he added.Meanwhile, Delhi Police detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Tuesday as they attempted to reach Jantar Mantar, police said.In a post on X, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke claimed that several other team members, including Ajinkya Shinde, had also been detained."Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police," Dipke said.“You cannot denotify the resistance, Narendra Modi,” Dipke said in the post.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday said protests would continue across the country until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigned. “You cannot denotify the resistance, Narendra Modi,” Dipke said in the post.

Article Title: Will hit streets again until PM Modi’s dictatorship ends, says CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke
Article Text:
Abhijeet also alleged that the police subjected him to mental harassment at a time when his grandmother had died.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday said his agitation would continue until what he called Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “dictatorship” came to an end.Speaking to the reporters following his recent arrest, Dipke accused the Delhi Police of mentally harassing him, violating his fundamental rights and preventing him from contacting his lawyer and family.“We will continue our agitation until Narendra Modi’s dictatorship ends. We will soon return to the streets,” Dipke said, reiterating his resolve to continue the protest despite the police action.Dipke’s mother, Anita, said the family would never forget how the govt’s actions prevented her son from seeing his grandmother for the last time. “We will not forget this until our last breath. Because of this govt, Abhijeet could not see his grandmother for the last time,” she said.Abhijeet alleged that Delhi Police violated his legal rights during his arrest by denying him access to his lawyer and brother. He challenged police to release the complete, unedited video of the arrest, claiming authorities withheld his whereabouts and details of the police station where he was detained from his family and legal representatives for an entire day.Abhijeet also alleged that the police subjected him to mental harassment at a time when his grandmother had died. “At around 3.30am, the police brought the arrest papers to me and pressured me to sign them, saying that I would be in jail for a long time and should call my parents and inform them,” he claimed, describing the episode as mental harassment of both him and his family.He also criticised the police for allegedly deploying women personnel during the arrest. Claiming that the move was intended to protect male officers from allegations of misconduct, Dipke said he and his associates were educated and knew how to treat women with respect. His allegations against Delhi Police could not be independently verified.Responding to questions about the possibility of externment from Maharashtra, Dipke targeted chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , questioning the state govt’s intentions and its handling of the issue.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday said his agitation would continue until what he called Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s ‘dictatorship’ came to an end. Dipke accused the Delhi Police of mentally harassing him, preventing him from contacting his lawyer and family.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Growing public sentiment against govt does not mean automatic win for opposition, says Chavan
Article Text:
Senior Congress member Prithviraj Chavan

Pune:

Fadnavis to campaign in Pune





Former chief minister and senior Congress member Prithviraj Chavan on Tuesday said there was a growing public sentiment against the govt but it did not mean an automatic victory for the opposition, stressing that the party workers would have to work hard to win the upcoming elections.He said, “Though the opposition to the govt is growing, it does not mean that the opposition will win elections automatically. We will have to still contest elections with our full might to win them. If we put in all our efforts, we will ensure victory,” the former chief minister said.Chavan visited Pune a day after the INDIA bloc’s protest march to Supreme Court in Delhi over the SIR row. The former chief minister participated in MVA’s campaign rally in Pune for the MVA’s candidates for graduate and teachers’ constituency polls. NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar addressed the rally virtually and appealed to MVA constituents to work collectively to ensure the victory of the alliance candidates.Chavan referred to protests by the INDIA bloc as well as Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and said, “There is a big shift in public sentiment across the country. The real face of the govt has been exposed and there is a growing sentiment against them. The younger generation especially is voicing its opposition to the govt.”Chavan told reporters after the campaign rally that chief election commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar would not resign despite the opposition mounting pressure on him.“If Kumar resigns, it will be an admission by the Modi govt that the elections were rigged. Therefore, he will try to hold on to the post as long as possible. The longer he stays in the post, the better for the opposition. It will further expose the govt,” he said.BJP has decided to focus on issues pertaining to teachers during the teachers and graduate constituencies’ polls, while chief minister Devendra Fadnavis will join the campaign in Pune on Wednesday.BJP’s Kaustubh Gawade is Mahayuti’s official candidate for the Pune teachers’ constituency, while Smita Jadhav has been nominated for the graduate constituency. Fadnavis will participate in the campaign rally for both the candidates in western Maharashtra.Ahead of Fadnavis’ visit, Mahayuti candidate Gawade said his focus would be to address the issues of teachers and relieve them of the unnecessary administrative duties. “I will raise my voice for a government resolution (GR) to curb non-teaching duties for govt teachers so that they can focus entirely on teaching,” he said.
Article Summary: Senior Congress member Prithviraj Chavan said there was a growing public sentiment against the govt. Chavan visited Pune a day after the INDIA bloc’s protest march to Supreme Court in Delhi over the SIR row. He said the party workers would have to work hard to win the upcoming elections.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu cops cite man's north Indian origins to claim he may flee, draws HC fire
Article Text:
Madras High Court





CHENNAI: Madras HC has pulled up the Tamil Nadu Police for opposing bail to an accused in a cheating case on the ground that he would flee since he was a "north Indian"."A person's place of origin is not a ground for apprehending that he will flee. The petitioner (accused) has lived and worked in Chennai for more than two decades. Such an averment ought not to have appeared in an affidavit sworn by a police officer," Justice N Ramesh said Tuesday. HC then granted conditional bail to the petitioner, Ankur Kumar Jani, and asked him to appear before the investigating officer as and when required.The issue pertains to an arrangement between FIITJEE Limited and Suguna PIP School, Coimbatore, to conduct integrated coaching for students preparing for the JEE and NEET examinations. As per the course scheme, each candidate was required to pay a refundable caution deposit of Rs 1 lakh. However, since the institutions failed to refund the deposit as promised, one person, who paid the deposit for his son, filed a complaint against Dinesh Kumar Goyal of FIITJEE Limited and Lakshmi Narayanasamy of Suguna PIP School. Jani was not named in the complaint or in the FIR. Police said he was named in view of an agreement dated Feb 26, 2011, which he is said to have signed on behalf of FIITJEE with the school. It was alleged the petitioner, along with others, has caused losses to 262 parents to the tune of Rs 2.62 crore. The first accused is said to be absconding, and the second accused has obtained anticipatory bail.On July 15, Ankur was arrested and had been in judicial custody since then.
Article Summary: Madras High Court pulls up Tamil Nadu Police for opposing bail to an accused in a cheating case on the ground that he would flee since he was a "north Indian" HC then granted conditional bail to the petitioner, Ankur Kumar Jani, and asked him to appear before the investigating officer as and when required.

Article Title: Former VAO sentenced to four years in jail for taking bribe of ₹1,000
Article Text:
Krishnagiri

:





A former village administrative officer (VAO) of Thuppuganapalli village in Hosur taluk was sentenced to four years’ rigorous imprisonment in a 2015 bribery case by the principal district court, in Krishnagiri, on Tuesday. The court also imposed a fine of ₹4,000 on him.According to court sources, a village resident had applied to transfer a patta from his mother’s name to his and his father’s names. “M Rajini, who was then village administrative officer, allegedly demanded ₹1,000 to process the application,” said a court official.The complainant approached the directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) in Krishnagiri, which laid a trap. Officials caught Rajini red-handed while accepting ₹1,000 from the complainant. He was arrested and remanded in judicial custody.Following investigation, DVAC filed a chargesheet against Rajini. Principal district judge VR Latha found him guilty and imposed the prison term and fine.
Article Summary: A former village administrative officer (VAO) of Thuppuganapalli village in Hosur taluk was sentenced to four years’ rigorous imprisonment in a 2015 bribery case by the principal district court, in Krishnagiri, on Tuesday. The court also imposed a fine of ₹4,000 on him. A village resident had applied to transfer a patta from his mother’s name to his and his father's names.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Kadayanallur DMK MLA, five others booked in land grabbing case
Article Text:
Kadayanallur DMK MLA, five others booked in land grabbing case

Tenkasi:





The Tenkasi district crime branch unit has registered a case against Kadayanallur DMK MLA T M Rajendran and five others for grabbing a land belonging to a differently abled person using forged documents.The FIR was registered on Oct 9 against Rajendran, his brother Chelladurai, VAO Arulmari, zonal deputy tahsildar Mohideen Pattani, land survey firka officer of Kurukkalpatti Usha and the sub-registrar of Melaneelithanallur. The case pertains to registrations allegedly made between 2008 and 2019.According to the FIR, complainant Murugaiah, a differently abled resident of Akkamalai in Coimbatore district, alleged that his family's ancestral land measuring about 9.7 acres in Thirumalapuram village was illegally transferred through fraudulent documentation.Murugaiah alleged that land standing in the joint names of his late father and uncle was sold and subsequently registered through a series of transactions without obtaining legal heir certificates or the consent of rightful heirs. He further claimed that the land was later converted into housing plots and sold to third parties.The complainant also alleged that portions of the land were encroached upon and included in property declarations submitted by the MLA during the 2026 assembly election.He accused certain revenue and registration officials of facilitating patta transfers and registrations without proper documentation.Based on the petition and supporting documents, the district crime branch registered the case.Police said further investigation is under way to verify the allegations and establish whether fraudulent land transactions had taken place.
Article Summary: Kadayanallur DMK MLA T M Rajendran, his brother Chelladurai, VAO Arulmari, zonal deputy tahsildar Mohideen Pattani, land survey firka officer of Kurukkalpatti Usha and the sub-registrar of Melaneelithanallur.

Article Title: Loadman sustains 70% burns in fireworks unit chemical blast
Article Text:
file picture

Virudhunagar

:





A loadman suffered 70% burn injuries after an aluminium powder tin being unloaded from a truck slipped and exploded at a fireworks unit in Virudhunagar district on Tuesday evening.According to police sources, the incident occurred around 4.30pm at Karthika Fireworks unit owned by Murugan in Gangarsevalpatti near Alangulam.Workers were engaged in manufacturing firecrackers required for the Diwali festival across more than 50 rooms.Police said aluminium powder tins were being unloaded from a truck when one of the tins accidentally slipped and exploded. The blast subsequently triggered an explosion in a nearby chemical godown, and one of the godowns was flattened. The truck was completely gutted by the fire.A loadman identified as Pulithurai, 25, of Sivakasi sustained more than 70% burn injuries. He was rushed to the Sivakasi govt hospital for treatment.A team from Vembakottai fire station was engaged in firefighting operations.Vembakottai police have registered a case.
Article Summary: Aluminium powder tins were being unloaded from a truck when one of the tins accidentally slipped and exploded. The blast subsequently triggered an explosion in a nearby chemical godown. A loadman identified as Pulithurai, 25, of Sivakasi sustained more than 70% burn injuries.

Article Title: Traffic affected on Salem-Madurai National Highway after trailer truck crashes near Rasipuram
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: Traffic was affected for more than an hour on the Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram in Namakkal district on Thursday afternoon after a trailer truck crashed while descending the Andagalur Gate flyover.No casualties or injuries were reported.The truck was carrying about 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. An officer at the Rasipuram police station said the driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover around 1.30pm. The truck hit a streetlight pole on the roadside. “The vehicle partially blocked the road, causing congestion and delays for motorists and commuters,” he said.Vehicles piled up for two kilometres on the NH. The Rasipuram police reached the spot after receiving information, regulated traffic and moved the truck to the roadside.Police registered a case and were investigating the circumstances leading to the crash.
Article Summary: Trailer truck crashes on Salem-Madurai National Highway near Rasipuram. Truck was carrying 60 tonnes of steel angles from Maharashtra to Karur. Driver lost control of the vehicle while descending the flyover. No casualties or injuries were reported.
